Attention Trading Partners: Refresher Training for New MaineCare Partner Portal

Sep 28, 2026

As a reminder, the new MaineCare Partner Portal is scheduled to go live on October 12, 2026, at 8:00 AM. The new portal will replace the current HealthPAS Online Portal and provide enhanced functionality to support Trading Partner operations. We are adding additional live, virtual instructor-led training sessions to help Trading Partners prepare for the transition. 

As a reminder, recorded training sessions, training materials, user guides, Q&A documents from training sessions, and supporting resources are available through the MMIS Learning Center and will continue to be available after go-live. 

Please share this training information with staff responsible for claims, authorizations, referrals, account maintenance, and portal administration activities. Staff should not wait for refresher training to become familiar with the materials. 

Key Reminders

  • Trading Partner Administrator (R7) accounts will be migrated to the new portal. 
  • Additional users will be invited and managed by Trading Partner Administrators after go-live. 
  • Trading Partner Administrators (R7 users) should prepare for portal access and account setup activities by reviewing the training materials available in the MMIS Learning Center before go-live.

MMIS Learning Center Access and Course Registration Instructions 

Use the following steps to register for MaineCare Partner Portal refresher training.  

  1. Go to the MMIS Learning Center.   
  2. Sign in using your existing account or select Sign Up to create a new account.  
    • If you need a new account, enter the enrollment key: De8pO9CBYXYB-aOCY8qp.  
    • Complete the required registration information to create your account. You may use your workplace address when registering.  
  3. From the Learner Dashboard, search for "TPT Refresher” using the Course Catalog or Search bar at the top of the window.  
  4. Click Choose Session and enroll in the session that best fits your schedule.  
  5. You will receive an enrollment confirmation email and a Microsoft Teams calendar invitation for each session.  
  6. On the day of training, join by selecting the Microsoft Teams link from:  
    • Your confirmation email 
    • Your Outlook or Teams calendar invitation 
    • The course listing in the MMIS Learning Center  

Important: Do not forward meeting invitations. Each participant must register through the MMIS Learning Center to receive training credit and access to course materials. 

Technical Support 

Please contact Jennifer Fehn or Haritha Chintada if you have questions regarding MMIS Learning Center access, training resources, or course registration.  

We look forward to supporting you as you prepare for the MaineCare Partner Portal launch.

Preparing for the changes to October payment cycles: 

The HealthPAS Online Portal has returned to its previous regular operating hours. Providers again have 24/7 access to the portal, for additional flexibility and time to submit claims outside of standard business hours.   

We strongly encourage providers to submit claims approaching timely filing limits in the next few weeks to avoid potential submission delays. The planned data freeze does not modify existing Medicaid timely filing requirements. Providers remain responsible for ensuring claims are submitted within the established timely filing guidelines. 

Other system access limitations: 

Providers can find other expected impacts of the data freeze in this FAQ. We have updated the FAQ as of September 21, 2026. Topics include: 

  • HealthPAS Online Portal, including impacts on submitting claims, submitting prior authorizations, and checking member eligibility 
  • Provider Enrollment Application (PEA) 
  • Value-Based Purchasing Management System (VMS) Portal

items.content_html: WASHINGTON – The Office of the United States Trade Representative has invoked the Rapid Response Labor Mechanism (RRM) in the United States-Mexico-Canada Agreement (USMCA) to review whether workers at Yokohama Tire Manufacturing Mexico, S.A. de C.V. (Yokohama), located in the state of Coahuila, Mexico, are being denied the right to freedom of association and collective bargaining. This follows the recent closure of the Yokohama tire manufacturing plant in Salem, Virginia and the layoff of nearly 600 American workers. The United States will suspend the liquidation of all entries of goods into this country from the Yokohama facility, which produces tires, until further notice.Today’s action demonstrates the Trump administration’s America First approach, which ensures our trade partners do not undermine worker protections to gain an unfair trade advantage or attract investment. The Secretary of Labor and United States Trade Representative co-chair the Interagency Labor Committee for Monitoring and Enforcement (ILC). On August 26, 2026, the ILC received an RRM petition from the Liga Sindical Obrera Mexicana (LSOM), a Mexican labor union, and the International Lawyers Assisting Workers Network (ILAW). The petition alleges that Yokohama is violating workers’ rights to freedom of association and collective bargaining by retaliating against workers for engaging in union activity. These actions include engaging in unequal treatment against LSOM supporters, the denial of access to the plant for LSOM special delegates while granting unrestricted access to the representatives of a competing union, irregularities leading up to a Certificate of Representation vote, unlawful dismissals, and non-compliance with the sectoral collective bargaining agreement for the rubber manufacturing industry (known as the “contrato ley”). The ILC reviews RRM petitions that it receives, and the accompanying information, within 30 days.  After conducting this review, the ILC determined that there is sufficient, credible evidence of a denial of rights enabling the good faith invocation of enforcement mechanisms. As a result, the United States Trade Representative has submitted a request to Mexico that Mexico review whether workers at Yokohama are being denied the right to freedom of association and collective bargaining. items.content_text: WASHINGTON – The U.S. Department of Labor today announced the award of $65 million in grants to consortia in seven states to help community colleges develop high-quality, short-term programs that can qualify for Workforce Pell funding. Administered by the department’s Employment and Training Administration, this sixth round of Strengthening Community Colleges Training Grants funding is awarded to statewide community college systems, or a consortia of community colleges to ensure effective development and expansion of the new programs and support the statewide coordination that is necessary for successful implementation of Workforce Pell Grants.       “Thanks to President Trump’s leadership, we are building an industry-driven education and workforce system that prepares Americans for the new, high-skilled, high-paying private-sector jobs his Administration is creating,” said Acting Secretary of Labor Keith Sonderling. “From advanced manufacturing to shipbuilding, Workforce Pell Grants will help community colleges equip Americans with the necessary skills and credentials, without unnecessary student debt.”The funding significantly contributes to national efforts to rapidly and effectively meet the hiring needs of employers, while also filling critical gaps in high-demand sectors, supporting skill gains, and worker mobility. Reminders in Preparation for Maine eCourts and eFiling in Cumberland County Courts

Date: 9/23/2026

On Monday, September 28, 2026, the Maine Judicial Branch is expanding Maine eCourts to all case types in Judicial Region 2, comprising Cumberland County Unified Criminal Docket (UCD), Cumberland County Superior Court, Portland District Court, and Bridgton District Court.

All case types -- civil, family, juvenile and criminal cases -- will be included in the transition from paper filing to electronic filing. As of Monday, September 28, all mandatory electronic filers pursuant to the Maine Rules of Electronic Court Systems (MRECS) will be required to eFile documents in these courts. Self-represented litigants (parties who do not have attorneys) who file fewer than six cases in a calendar year will not be required to eFile.

Court Closures and Emergency Filing Procedures
To prepare for the implementation of Maine eCourts and eFiling on September 28, Region 2 courts are currently operating on a modified schedule and have emergency filing procedures in place. In addition, all Region 2 courts will be closed from 8 a.m. to noon the week of September 28th. Please refer to the schedule of closures and emergency procedures during these closings.

ShareFile Discontinued in Region 2 Courts
The ShareFile platform used in Region 2 courts will be disabled for all criminal, civil violation, juvenile filings, and GAL vouchers, at 2:00 p.m. on Thursday, September 24. Starting Monday, September 28, attorneys must instead use eFileMaine. Please note, attorney vouchers filed pursuant to the Standing Order regarding Payment to Court-Appointed Counsel will continue to be accepted by ShareFile for a grace period of 60 days.

Training Resources
For attorneys and staff who are new to using eFileMaine, we highly recommend viewing the recorded videos, particularly the video excerpts, available on the Maine eCourts Trainings and Resources web page. In addition to the recordings, the information and resources available on the Maine eCourts Trainings and Resources web page offer guidance for setting up your eFileMaine account and instructions to eFile documents successfully.

Personal Identifying Information (PII) Attachment (CR-CV-JV-297)
Pursuant to the Maine Rules of Electronic Court Systems (MRECS) filers are responsible for omitting or redacting nonpublic information in electronically filed documents. If the filer decides to omit rather than redact, the personal identifying information must be included on this form.

The PII form should be uploaded as an attachment to the associated filing document, in the same way that an exhibit is submitted.

Online Fine Payments
As of September 28th, parties who wish to make criminal fine payments online for cases in Cumberland County will be directed to the new online payment portal, Maine eCourts Criminal Fines and Fees. Visit Maine eCourts: Pay a Court Fine to learn more.

Support
Support for eFiling is available by emailing ecourtshelp@courts.maine.gov or by calling (207) 213-2813, Monday through Thursday from 10 a.m. to 2 p.m.

For more information on Maine eCourts and eFiling, visit: https://www.courts.maine.gov/ecourts/index.html
